URBAN BRICK APARTMENT ROW — a city block of three-story flat-roofed brick apartments with fire-escape balconies, each balcony dressed with a glowing pumpkin or strand of purple lights, a broad concrete sidewalk below busy with fallen ginkgo leaves, a corner bodega awning trimmed in orange foil fringe, amber streetlamps casting overlapping pools of warm pixel light.

HILLSIDE VICTORIAN TERRACE — terraced Victorian homes climbing a steep residential hill, each dwelling's porch a full story above its neighbor's roofline, pocket gardens between retaining walls strung with paper lantern globes in orange and white, carved pumpkins on each terrace-wall ledge, the street below receding in warm lamplight while the hill's peak fades into deep violet.

LAKESHORE CRAFTSMAN DOCK STREET — a lakeshore lane of craftsman-style cottages with wide overwater decks and shingled rooflines, dock posts capped with small carved pumpkins, dock lanterns warming the still water below, leafy birch trees lining the landward side of the street catching the last pink of dusk, the far lake surface a dark mirror of the fading sky.

SUBURBAN COTTAGE CUL-DE-SAC — a rounded dead-end of small storybook-style cottages with arched front doors and round-topped windows, each tiny lawn edged in solar-powered pumpkin-shaped stake lights, a communal island garden at the cul-de-sac center ringed with potted orange mums and a single grinning pumpkin on a pedestal, the whole block lit in a gentle amber-and-purple evening glow.

CRAFTSMAN BUNGALOW ROW — a gently curving residential street of single-story craftsman bungalows with deep covered porches and exposed rafter tails, low hedges trimmed square along the sidewalk, carved pumpkins glowing amber on every front step, string lights looping porch-to-porch, pixel-dither shadows pooling in the sidewalk cracks at dusk.

VICTORIAN CORNER BLOCK — a tall narrow Victorian row turning a gaslit corner, steeply gabled turrets casting long triangle shadows, wrought-iron fences strung with paper-bat garlands, carved pumpkins lined along stone stoops, a corner lamppost just buzzing to life, depth receding down the block in warm amber window-glow.

COLONIAL TWO-STORY STREET — a straight suburban avenue of symmetrical two-story colonial homes with black-shuttered windows and white clapboard siding, matching jack-o-lanterns flanking every front door, leaf piles raked to curb edges, carriage-style porch lights warming the front walks, the block receding into a soft violet dusk at the far end.

FARMHOUSE COUNTRY LANE — a winding gravel lane edged by split-rail fences draped in dried cornstalks, a weathered clapboard farmhouse set back from the road, a leaning barn silhouetted against an orange-streaked dusk sky, a hand-painted pumpkin stand at the gate, the lane dissolving into dark tree line at the far horizon.

BROWNSTONE STOOP ROW — a dense urban block of red-brick brownstones with wide stone stoops and iron railings, potted mums and small pumpkins on every landing, wrought-iron fences linked by orange ribbon, tall street trees dropping pixel-dithered leaf shadows on the sidewalk, windows glowing warm behind gauzy curtain-curtains as dusk thickens.

SPLIT-LEVEL SUBURBAN CUL-DE-SAC — a gentle circular cul-de-sac of split-level homes with two-toned brick-and-siding facades, driveways dotted with inflatable ghost decorations soft-glowing white, maples at peak orange color overhead, a central island of grass with a cluster of pumpkins, the curve of the street creating layered depth back to the last house.

RANCH-HOUSE BLOCK — a long flat suburban block of wide single-story ranch homes with attached garages and broad front lawns, hay bales and pumpkin clusters at each driveway entrance, low coach lights warming concrete front walks, the road stretching straight into a darkening amber horizon, sprinkler heads catching the last sliver of sunset.

COTTAGE LANE — a narrow winding lane of small storybook cottages with steeply pitched roofs and low picket fences painted white, window boxes still holding late marigolds, tiny carved pumpkins perched on fence posts every few feet, porch lanterns just clicking on, the lane curving away through overgrown hedges into soft evening shadow.

SMALL-TOWN MAIN STREET BLOCK — a compact downtown block of two-story brick-front shops with flat cornices and awnings, window displays full of paper ghosts and orange tinsel, jack-o-lanterns lined along the curb between old parking meters, streetlamps switching on one by one, the upper-floor apartment windows glowing warm above the storefronts.

APARTMENT COURTYARD BLOCK — a U-shaped brick apartment complex enclosing a shared communal courtyard, strings of orange lights looping between the buildings, a cluster of carved pumpkins around the central courtyard bench, residents' windows framing warm golden light, the deep courtyard perspective drawing the eye back to a lit archway on the far wall.

HILLSIDE STAIR-STREET — a steep stair-street climbing a tile-roofed hillside neighborhood, houses stacked up the slope in terraced rows, each landing decorated with a small pumpkin grouping, wrought-iron handrails wound with plastic spider webbing, the stairway receding in perspective up into a bruised-purple sky with the first stars appearing.

LAKESIDE COTTAGE ROW — a short row of weathered shingle cottages facing a dark glassy lake, dock posts strung with orange fairy lights reflecting on the water, carved pumpkins glowing on each narrow front porch, a canoe pulled up on the shore, the far tree line a solid black silhouette against a deep teal dusk sky.

CAPE COD SHINGLE STREET — a breezy coastal street of grey-shingled cape cod homes with dormers and shuttered windows, low stone walls lining the front yards, salt-weathered pumpkins on every stoop, weathervanes pointing west in an evening breeze, the street sloping gently toward a glimpse of dark ocean at the far end of the block.

TUDOR REVIVAL BLOCK — a stately block of Tudor-revival homes with steep cross-gabled roofs, decorative half-timbering, and tall grouped chimney stacks, autumn ivy blazing red across the facade, carved lanterns in arched niches beside heavy oak doors, leaded window panes glowing amber, the whole block bathed in the last flat gold light of dusk.

TRAILER PARK LANE — a friendly lane of neat mobile homes with skirted bases and metal awnings draped in orange-and-purple string lights, handmade scarecrows staked in small front yards, pumpkins arranged on wooden deck steps, a communal fire pit at the lane's end with a faint orange glow, utility poles strung with paper-bat garlands.

SMALL-TOWN SQUARE — a classic town square ringed by two-story brick shops and a painted gazebo centered on a grassy common, strands of harvest lights crisscrossing from gazebo to rooftop, carved pumpkins lining the gazebo railing, park benches scattered with fallen leaves, lampposts dressed in black ribbon bows switching on as the sky deepens to indigo.

ADOBE SOUTHWESTERN BLOCK — a single-story block of flat-roofed adobe homes with rounded parapet walls and terracotta accents, luminaria bags lining every walkway in warm flickering rows, dried chili ristras sharing hooks with paper skeleton garlands, a turquoise-painted garden gate open to a glowing courtyard beyond, the sky a vivid coral band above the flat rooftops.

NEW ENGLAND GREEN — a wide grassy common flanked by white clapboard colonials, a white chapel with a slim steeple visible at the far end of the green, maples raining orange leaves across the pixel-dithered grass, carved pumpkins placed along the stone border walls, gas-style lampposts switching on in a line toward the chapel silhouette.

TOWNHOUSE ROW WITH SHARED STOOPS — a tidy urban block of three-story townhouses sharing wide brick stoops and continuous iron railings, each stoop decorated with mismatched pumpkin groupings and potted ornamental kale, window boxes trailing dried vines, upper floors glowing warm behind half-drawn curtains, the shared sidewalk perspective drawing depth down a long brick facade.

WOODED CUL-DE-SAC EDGE — a quiet cul-de-sac where the houses on the far arc back directly onto a dense stand of dark oaks, the tree canopy closing overhead in layered pixel-dither shadows, orange lights strung from porch to porch across the street, carved pumpkins glowing extra bright against the deep blackness of the tree line behind them.
